The '''2022–23 FIS Cross-Country World Cup''', organized by the [[International Ski Federation]] was the 42nd [[FIS Cross-Country World Cup|World Cup]] in [[cross-country skiing (sport)|cross-country skiing]] for men and women. The season started on 25 November 2022 in [[Rukatunturi|Ruka]], Finland and concluded on 26 March 2023 in [[Lahti]], Finland.<ref>{{cite web|title=FIS Cross-Country World Cup 2022/23|url=https://assets.fis-ski.com/image/upload/v1664805256/fis-prod/assets/WC_Calendar_CC_2022-23_Oct2022.pdf|publisher=fis-ski.com|access-date=30 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="FIS rules">{{cite web|url=https://assets.fis-ski.com/image/upload/v1654174819/fis-prod/assets/World_Cup_Rules_Cross-Country_2022-23.pdf|title=Rules for the FIS Cross-Country World Cup 2022/2023|website=[[International Ski Federation|FIS]]|access-date=2 June 2022}}</ref>

The season featured a break in February and March for the [[FIS Nordic World Ski Championships 2023|World Championships in Planica]].

[[Johannes Høsflot Klæbo]] from Norway and [[Natalya Nepryayeva]] from Russia were the defending overall champions from the [[2021–22 FIS Cross-Country World Cup|2021–22 season]]. Nepryayeva couldn't defend her title because of the decision of the [[International Ski Federation|FIS Council]], that Russia and Belarus have been suspended for this World Cup season due to the [[2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Decisions of the fis council at its autumn meeting 2022|url=https://www.fis-ski.com/en/international-ski-federation/news-multimedia/news-2022/decisions-of-the-fis-council-at-its-autumn-meeting-2022|publisher=fis-ski.com|access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref>

[[Johannes Høsflot Klæbo|Klæbo]] defended the title and won his fourth World Cup title. Women's overall victory award went to Norwegian [[Tiril Udnes Weng]] for the first time.
